cues.text: A Fortune Given Away
Born in 1499 (some sources say 1500) at Almodóvar del Campo in Spain to a wealthy family, John began studying law at Salamanca at fourteen but soon lost interest.
He returned home for years of austere private devotion before pursuing philosophy and theology at Alcalá under the noted Dominican theologian Domingo de Soto.
Ordained a priest in 1525, he sold the entire inheritance left him by his deceased parents and distributed the proceeds to the poor.
Redirected to Andalusia
John had prepared to sail as a missionary to Mexico.
Instead, the Archbishop of Seville persuaded him to devote his considerable gifts to evangelizing Andalusia .

This southern Spanish region, much of which had been reconquered centuries earlier while Granada had fallen only recently, still had substantial need of Christian renewal, and Christian practice remained in real need of renewal.
Beginning his preaching mission in 1529, he labored there for the rest of his life.
Investigated by the Inquisition
John's uncompromising sermons against wealth, vice, and worldliness stirred real opposition among some of his hearers.
He was briefly imprisoned and investigated by the Inquisition on suspicion of heresy—a trial from which he emerged fully cleared in 1533, his popularity, if anything, only enhanced by the episode.
A Formative Spiritual Director
John of Ávila's influence extended far beyond his own preaching through the extraordinary number of future saints shaped by his spiritual counsel and direction.
These included St. Teresa of Ávila , St. John of God , St. Francis Borgia, and others.
His friendship and encouragement were also credited with helping the newly founded Society of Jesus establish itself in Spain.
Founder of Colleges
Convinced that the clergy's own formation was central to any lasting reform, John founded colleges to train diocesan priests.
Most notably, he founded the University of Baeza in 1538 and produced widely read spiritual writings.
These included a treatise addressed to the Council of Trent on the reform of clerical life, that shaped Spanish spirituality for generations after his death.
Legacy
Suffering ill health for the last eighteen years of his life, worn down by the cumulative rigors of his apostolate, John died at Montilla in 1569.
Beatified in 1893 and canonized in 1970 by Pope Paul VI, he was declared a Doctor of the Church in 2012 by Pope Benedict XVI.
He was one of a select company across the Church's whole history to receive that title, in recognition of his enduring influence on the spiritual formation of priests.
